verdict: Kinsta: Choose Kinsta when managed WordPress hosting is the job — not a Plesk/DirectAdmin panel licence, and not WP Engine by default. Scores use the IT & Development editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-18 — not hands-on product testing.
bestFor: Teams that want managed WordPress hosting without a panel licence
Buyers comparing Kinsta $35 Single to WP Engine Essential and Cloudways Flexible
Orgs that will treat $35 as ongoing TCO, not a promo month
notIdealFor: Admins buying Plesk or DirectAdmin licences for servers they already own
Multi-cloud VM hosting as the primary shape (Cloudways)
tradeoffs: Per-agent vs per-host vs per-seat vs per-GB pricing models
Module stacking and consumption overages vs single-SKU floors
Free tiers vs enterprise SSO/audit gates
Landscape-adjacent tools vs primary job-cluster peers on best pages
recommendation: Choose Kinsta when managed WordPress hosting is the job — not a Plesk/DirectAdmin panel licence, and not WP Engine by default. Compare WP Engine for WordPress-specialist managed hosting; Cloudways for managed multi-cloud VMs; Plesk only on landscape pages for panel licences.
editorialNotes: IT industry Tier-A batch. Approved on it-development-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=hosting-providers. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

No meaningful ITSM/dev AI copilot — scored low; hosting job rarely needs AI scoring depth.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the eight IT editorial criteria using category weights (IT job fit 16, workflow depth 14, ease of use 12, integrations 12, admin/security 12, value 12, AI 12, scalability 10), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — ITSM, observability, source control, hosting panels, and web-data platforms are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
